newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to send extra $3 million for Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to send extra $3 million for Zaire refugees.

text.p: The State Department said on Monday it was donating another $3 million to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees to support the repatriation of refugees in eastern Zaire.
Spokesman John Dinger said in a statement that further contributions would be announced shortly in response to a U.N. emergency appeal.

U.S. officials described the new aid as part of a continuing effort to alleviate the almost three-year-long refugee crisis in the area, which has been complicated by a rebel uprising there since last October.

Over a million refugees arrived in Zaire from neighbouring Rwanda in 1994. More than 600,000 returned to Rwanda last November soon after the outbreak of Zaire's civil war, and since then UNHCR says it has repatriated 140,000 others.

Dinger said UNHCR had now been able to reach some refugees who moved deeper into Zaire after rebel forces overran their camps late last year, and was arranging their repatriation to Rwanda, a course Washington strongly supports.
The new U.S. funding is from the State Department's migration and refugee assistance appropriation, Dinger said.
The United States has contributed more than $1 billion for humanitarian assistance in the Great Lakes region of Central Africa since late 1993, he said.
